name: Spyglass short-range radar (Anduril / Numerica)
description: Ku-band phased array with simultaneous transmit and receive. Numerica states detection and track of small autonomous UAS beyond 3.5 km. Demonstrated in the JCO-recommended SAIC C-sUAS-as-a-Service at Yuma, Sep 2022. Now an Anduril product in Lattice.

detectRangeM.note: Inventory records 3500 m (beyond three and a half km); the seed value is kept

rangeAccuracyM.note: Class median of the sourced surveillance radars: lib-r8ss 3; median 3 m.

azimuthAccuracyDeg.note: Class median of the sourced surveillance radars: lib-r8ss 0.8; median 0.8 deg.

elevationAccuracyDeg.note: Class median of the sourced surveillance radars: lib-r8ss 3; median 3 deg.

falseAlarmRatePerScan.note: Planning factor: PLACARD_PFA 1e-6 (src/model/types.ts) times about 1e6 range-azimuth-Doppler cells per scan of a 360° surveillance volume gives about one false alarm per scan over the whole coverage; this 90° sector panel searches about half the cells and is recorded at 0.5. No vendor publishes a false-alarm rate.

dwellTimeS.note: Planning factor: Anduril / Numerica publishes no dwell or CPI. An electronically scanned radar sets its dwell in the beam schedule rather than by beamwidth over scan rate; the literature CPI of 20 ms for X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs is used. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler.

pulsesPerDwell.note: Planning factor: Anduril / Numerica publishes no PRF or pulse count. 20 ms dwell at the literature 5 kHz PRF gives 100 pulses coherently integrated. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler.
